Copernicus Marine Toolbox API

Author

Carlo Zampieri

Published

May 28, 2026

This document will give you a brief introduction on the Copernicus Marine Toolbox, which is a Python package to browse and download products from the Copernicus Marine Data Store.

Important

The Copernicus Marine Toolbox can be used from the terminal or as a Python module. This document just give an introduction on how to run the toolbox functions in Python, but it does not explain how to get or use Python itself. For more information on Python visit the official webpage, or this page to know how to use Python within your RStudio environment.

Installation

This tool is compatible with Windows, MacOS and Linux running Python v3.10 to v3.13.

There are several ways to install the toolbox in your computer. Here we will see only the one using pip, but if you prefer another way, you can check the complete installation tutorial.

Type the following line in your terminal:

python -m pip install copernicusmarine

To make sure the toolbox has been successfully installed, execute this line in your terminal:

copernicusmarine --version

or these commands in your Python environment:

import copernicusmarine
copernicusmarine.__version__

Credentials configuration

As for downloading through the website, you need to login in your personal account. You can do that easily by using the login command in Python:

import copernicusmarine
copernicusmarine.login(
  username="youruserid",
  password="yourpassword")
Note

You need to login just once!

Explore catalogue and metadata

The function describe allows to explore the CMEMS catalogue and the metadata of the available products. For example:

import copernicusmarine
copernicusmarine.describe(
  product_id="MEDSEA_MULTIYEAR_BGC_006_008",
  disable_progress_bar=True
  )
CopernicusMarineCatalogue(products=[CopernicusMarineProduct(title='Mediterranean Sea Biogeochemistry Reanalysis', product_id='MEDSEA_MULTIYEAR_BGC_006_008', thumbnail_url='https://mdl-metadata.s3.waw3-1.cloudferro.com/metadata/thumbnails/MEDSEA_MULTIYEAR_BGC_006_008.jpg', description='The Mediterranean Sea biogeochemical reanalysis at 1/24° of horizontal resolution (ca. 4 km) covers the period from Jan 1999 to 1 month to the present and is produced by means of the MedBFM3 model system. MedBFM3, which is run by OGS (IT), includes the transport model OGSTM v4.0 coupled with the biogeochemical flux model BFM v5 and the variational data assimilation module 3DVAR-BIO v2.1 for surface chlorophyll. MedBFM3 is forced by the physical reanalysis (MEDSEA_MULTIYEAR_PHY_006_004 product run by CMCC) that provides daily forcing fields (i.e., currents, temperature, salinity, diffusivities, wind and solar radiation). The ESA-CCI database of surface chlorophyll concentration (CMEMS-OCTAC REP product) is assimilated with a weekly frequency. \n\nCossarini, G., Feudale, L., Teruzzi, A., Bolzon, G., Coidessa, G., Solidoro C., Amadio, C., Lazzari, P., Brosich, A., Di Biagio, V., and Salon, S., 2021. As you can see the output is a bit messy and you might prefer to use the Copernicus Marine Data Store webpage to explore the catalogue more easily.

If you want to know more on the function describe and its usage, visit this page.

Subset and download

The web interface for downloading data from the Copernicus Marine Data Store limits you at maximum 1GB files. To bypass this limit you can split the data you need in smaller chunks (for example by time or space) or use the Copernicus Marine Toolbox! The function subset allows you to subset and download the data you need without any size limit.

For example, if I want to download the daily surface temperature of 2024 in the northern Adriatic Sea from the Mediterranean Sea Physics Reanalysis product, I will execute the following code:

import copernicusmarine
copernicusmarine.subset(
  dataset_id = "cmems_mod_med_phy-temp_my_4.2km_P1D-m",
  variables = ["thetao"],
  minimum_longitude = 12,
  maximum_longitude = 15.5,
  minimum_latitude = 43.5,
  maximum_latitude = 46,
  start_datetime="2024-01-01T00:00:00",
  end_datetime="2024-12-31T00:00:00",
  minimum_depth=1.0182366371154785,
  maximum_depth=1.0182366371154785,
  output_directory = "C:Users/User/Download/",
  output_filename = "nadr_sst_daily_2024.nc",
  force_download = True
)
Note

To fill the arguments of the describe function you need to know the dataset id and other specs of the product from which you wish to download the data. I suggest to first explore the product and get an idea of what you need, by visiting the Copernicus Marine Data Store webpage.

An easier way to know how to fill the function arguments is to select the dataset, variables, spatial and temporal extent in the data store webpage and then click on “Automate”. A pop-up window will show you how to code the data request.

If you want to download data from multiple datasets in once, you can iterate the code shown above using a for loop as in this file.
